The served body is UTF-8 WITH BOM and LF line endings (0 CR bytes, 0 form feeds, no page footers); collapse() does not strip the byte-order mark, so the capture keeps it as line 1 (bytes ef bb bf) and that line holds no document text.

quotes.quote: For web-based services, organizations MUST place the "security.txt" file under the "/.well-known/" path
quotes.location: L330-L331; Section 3 'Location of the security.txt File' (heading L329), the MUST that places the file under the '/.well-known/' path per [RFC8615]. The paragraph continues with the legacy top-level-or-redirect allowance and the 'the one in the "/.well-known/" path MUST be used' rule (L333-L337).

quotes.quote: It is RECOMMENDED that the value of this field be less than a year into the future to avoid staleness.
quotes.location: L270-L272; Section 2.5.5 'Expires' (heading L265), the strength and direction of the staleness bound (RECOMMENDED, less than a year - not a MUST). The field itself MUST always be present and MUST NOT appear more than once (L273); Section 5.3 (L541-L545) makes the Expires field the mechanism by which a publisher declares the data stale.

quotes.quote: When the value of this field is an email address, it is RECOMMENDED that encryption be used (as per Section 2.5.4).
quotes.location: L235-L237; Section 2.5.3 'Contact' (heading L224), the encryption RECOMMENDATION for a mailto contact value. The referenced 'Encryption' field is Section 2.5.4 (heading L247): the value MUST be a URI pointing to where the key can be retrieved, keys MUST NOT appear in the field itself (L249-L251).
